accuracy.evidence: Facts checked against NOAA Ocean Service and the NOAA Coral Reef Conservation Program pages 'What are corals?' and 'Coral reef ecosystems': coral polyps are cnidarians (relatives of jellyfish and anemones) that catch plankton with stinging tentacles, mostly at night; reef-building polyps secrete calcium carbonate (limestone) skeletons and live on top of the skeletons of earlier generations; zooxanthellae algae live in the polyp tissue, photosynthesise, share food and give colour, so reef-building corals need warm, clear, shallow, sunlit water; heat stress makes polyps expel the algae and turn white (bleaching) and corals can starve if it lasts; reefs cover under 1% of the ocean floor but support about 25% of marine species. Growth of 'often about a centimetre a year' sits inside NOAA's 0.3–2 cm per year for massive corals (branching corals grow faster), and the lab's 100 years per metre layer uses that rate. Parameterised answers (100n, nm, n−m, n) were enumerated by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented child ideas about coral (Ocean Literacy principle 5 notes and teacher guides from NOAA and the Great Barrier Reef Foundation): coral is a rock or a plant (predict in step 1 and challenge tags rock/plant), the whole reef is alive (challenge tag allalive, the grey 'old cups' layers in step 2), animals do not need light so depth does not matter (step 3 predict, deep/dark and muddy zone feedback), and white coral is clean and healthy (very hot zone shows bleaching; challenge tag white). Each wrong answer gets its own message.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed. Existing ocean labs are 643 What ocean animals need (flagseaneed), 653 Ocean animal variety (flagovar) and 893 Fossils as evidence (flagfossev); none open polyps, stack limestone generations, move one coral between light and temperature conditions with a bleaching outcome, or match reef animals to reef structures. Only this lab models how a reef is built by animals and why it needs sunlit water.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover each idea by doing: tapping bumps reveals tentacled animals; each tap of 'Grow 100 years' turns the old living layer to grey limestone, so after five taps they see only the top is alive and 500 years made 5 m; dragging the coral to dark, cold, muddy and hot water gives a reason it fails before warm, clear, shallow water works; housing six animals in six different reef features shows why variety is so high; the banner only states the rule after the task is won.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'What is coral really?' with 'A kind of rock' and 'A sea plant' (the two common beliefs), 'How fast does a reef grow?' with 'It does not grow: it is rock' and 'a metre a week', and 'Do polyps need sunlight too?' with 'No: they are animals, so light does not matter'. The lab then shows polyps, slow layers and the dark-water failure, and the task message says whether the prediction was right.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; each wrong option carries a tag with its own feedback: rock (polyps build limestone cups), plant (algae are the plant-like partner, polyps are animals), cold and dark (algae need warm, clear, sunny water), white (bleached coral has lost its algae and can starve), trees and rain (the name is about variety of life), allalive (only the top layer is alive). Correct answers build a streak.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores Flesch-Kincaid 3.3 (limit 6.5) and adult text 8.8 (limit 9.5). Sentences are short and concrete, the curriculum words polyp, tentacles, plankton, limestone, algae, habitat and bleaching are each explained the first time they appear, and lab buttons use plain verbs ('Open bump 1', 'Grow 100 years', 'Put coral in: Cold water').

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and the explanation shares under 12% of 6-word shingles with every other lesson. Every kid paragraph carries one idea (animal, building, algae and light, habitat variety), the adult text gives standards, the task sequence and common mistakes, and no sentence repeats template text from other reviews or lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px wide screenshots in dark and light themes at every step before and after Show me (/workspace/wn2353-shots/reef-*): the banner, zone labels, animal and home cards, reef layers and the feedback strip all fit without clipping; the canvas is 1.3 times taller than wide on phones so the 2-column place grid and 3-column home grid stay readable; polyp tap areas were enlarged to about 48 px and every action also has a full-width button.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every task completes with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes and there are no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Open bump n, Grow 100 years, Put coral in, Pick then Put the animal at, reason cards), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the state (layers, places tried, animals housed), and feedback is also announced through c.say.
